predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Gwent, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands: south-east Wales between the Wye and the Usk

successors.name: Kingdom of Morgannwg
successors.text: what remained of Gwent in 1074, taken by Caradog ap Gruffudd from Cadwgan ap Meurig

successors.name: Norman England
successors.text: the Marcher lordships of Abergavenny, Caerleon, Monmouth, Striguil (Chepstow) and Usk

ledger.x: 577: Cliopatria adds one cell (253 km2) on the Wye in Archenfield.
926: Athelstan and the Welsh kings fix the border at the Wye.
942: Morgan Hen unites Gwent and Glywysing as Morgannwg.
975: Gwent is separate from Morgannwg again.

1074: Gwent passes to Caradog and the fight with the Normans passes to Morgannwg (the Gwent page has most of Gwent firmly under Norman control when Caradog died in 1081; the Norman invasion page a castle at Caerleon by 1086).
1074: Caradog ap Gruffudd takes what remains of Gwent from Cadwgan ap Meurig; the Glywysing page's infobox has the union 1063-1074 and the name Morgannwg from 1075.
1074: the Kingdom of Gwent ends in Caradog's Morgannwg.

wars.name: Canute's invasion of Gwent
wars.outcome: Canute invaded Gwent in 1034; the page records no territorial result.

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffydd won control of Gwent and Morgannwg in 1055; in 1056 he campaigned from near Monmouth and defeated Ralph, Earl of Hereford; after his death in 1063 Caradog ap Gruffudd re-established an independent Gwent.

wars.name: Harold's invasion of Gwent
wars.outcome: Harold of Hereford tried to set up a base at Portskewett and Caradog razed it.

wars.name: Norman invasion of south-east Wales
wars.outcome: The Normans sacked south-east Wales and parts of Gwent in 1070 and had a castle at Striguil by 1071; Caradog died in 1081 with most of Gwent firmly under Norman control; Caerleon castle stood by 1086.
